title: The Quiet Thief
primary_metric: required monthly retirement contribution (USD, in today's real purchasing power) for the late starter to match the early starter's real ending balance

options.A: Commit to the Bridge Plan — raise the monthly contribution to the exact higher amount required, in today's real dollars, to match Priya's target balance by retiring at the same age as Priya
options.B: Commit to the Extended Plan — keep a lower monthly contribution and match that same real target balance only by working two additional years past Priya's retirement age

sources.claim: Long-run average annual U.S. inflation rate (Consumer Price Index, CPI-U)
sources.title: Consumer Price Index, 1913-
sources.note: Derived as a compound annual growth rate from the page's own published CPI-U index values (1913 index = 9.9; 2025 index = 321.9, both 1982-84=100 base): (321.9 / 9.9)^(1/112) - 1 = 3.1%/year. Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis is a primary, official publisher of this BLS-sourced CPI series -- not a third-party aggregator. Cross-checked against multiple independent secondary aggregators (usinflationcalculator.com, rateinflation.com) that similarly describe the average since 1913 as approximately 3.1-3.2%/year, corroborating this derivation.

_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC §4

This case exists to close that topic gap.

Only 6 skills in the entire spine currently have n==0 (number-sense-depth, number-sense-digit, geometry-how-to-find-the-volume-of-a-sphere, calculus-how-to-use-the-quotient-rule-to-differentiate-a-quotient-of-functions, calculus-taylor-series, calculus-how-to-find-the-taylor-series-of-a-function-at-a-point) -- none in the Advanced Operations/Advanced Numbers group this case exercises, and none reachable from any of this case's deliverables (D1-D5 force percent-to-number conversion, exponential-expression evaluation with fractional and whole-number exponents, order-of-operations sequencing around an exponent, and percent-of-a-number comparisons; they never touch place-value digits, sphere volume, the quotient rule, or Taylor series). This case was approved from the concept sheet specifically to reinforce advanced-operations-how-to-evaluate-an-exponential-expression and the thin advanced-operations-how-to-evaluate-an-expression-with-multiple-operations-with-exponents-order skill (n=2, tied for the thinnest how-to in the Advanced Operations/Exponents group) by forcing both repeatedly across D1-D3 and D5, not to close a zero-coverage gap -- consistent with the disclosed-reinforcement precedent in cases/the-two-offers/case.json and cases/the-bracket-bet/case.json. Flag for case-readiness to confirm this disclosed deviation rather than treat it as an undisclosed zero-new-coverage defect.

deliverables.text: The real rate of return, derived, not given: convert Appendix C's sourced nominal average return and sourced average inflation rate from percents to numbers, derive the annual real (inflation-adjusted) rate of return using real = (1+nominal)/(1+inflation) - 1, then convert that annual real rate into an equivalent monthly rate using (1+annual real rate)^(1/12) - 1, with the exponential expression evaluated step by step.

Priya's real retirement balance: using FV = PMT x [((1+r)^n - 1)/r] with D1's derived monthly real rate and Appendix A's contribution and months, compute Priya's real account balance at retirement, with the (1+r)^n exponent term evaluated as its own explicit step.

The Bridge Plan's required contribution: rearrange D2's formula to PMT = FV x r / [(1+r)^n - 1] and compute, using Appendix B's Bridge Plan months, the exact monthly contribution required; state this amount as a percent increase over Priya's own contribution from Appendix A.

The Extended Plan's required contribution and the margin between the two plans: repeat D3's method using Appendix B's Extended Plan months, then compute the percent by which the Extended Plan's required contribution is lower than the Bridge Plan's D3 figure.

The nominal-rate trap: recompute D3's Bridge Plan contribution using Appendix C's un-adjusted nominal rate in place of D1's derived real rate, show both figures side by side, and compute the percent by which the nominal-rate figure understates the true required contribution.

balance.argument_a: CONFIRMED by case-research. The Bridge Plan is the only path that actually delivers Priya's exact real target balance by Jordan's originally intended retirement age -- it requires $817.00/month (about 2.04x Priya's $400/month), but it closes the ten-year gap fully and on the original timeline, without betting on two additional working years going as planned.
balance.argument_b: CONFIRMED by case-research. The Extended Plan reaches the identical real target balance for a meaningfully lower monthly commitment -- $705.38/month (about 1.76x Priya's $400/month), a real, computed 13.66% reduction from the Bridge Plan's D3 figure -- by trading two additional years of account growth for a smaller monthly sacrifice starting today, a genuine and common real-world trade-off between money now and time later.
balance.margin_basis: Real annual rate of return = (1+0.10)/(1+0.031) - 1 = 6.6925% [S2, S3 combined, D1]. Real monthly rate = (1.066925)^(1/12) - 1 = 0.5413%/month. Priya's real target balance (504 months at $400/month) = FV = 400 x [(1.005413)^504 - 1]/0.005413 = $1,048,768.04 (D2). Bridge Plan (384 months): PMT_A = FV x r / [(1+r)^384 - 1] = $817.00/month (D3). Extended Plan (408 months): PMT_B = FV x r / [(1+r)^408 - 1] = $705.38/month (D4). margin_pct = (PMT_A - PMT_B)/PMT_A x 100 = 13.66%. Nominal-rate trap (D5): using the nominal 10% rate instead of the derived real rate for the Bridge Plan gives PMT_naive = $415.79/month, a 49.11% understatement of the true $817.00 figure. Full arithmetic in RESEARCH_LOG.md and sensitivity_model.py.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Chosen narrative constants to set up a clean, round ten-year late start -- the exact scenario the concept behind this case is built to examine. Not tied to any real person.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Every case computation scales with the size of this gap; a smaller gap would shrink the dollar difference between Priya's and Jordan's plans, and a larger gap would grow it, but it does not change the direction of the case's point -- starting later always costs more in real terms.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Both savers' planned monthly contribution amount
modeling_assumptions.basis: A common, round, early-career monthly retirement-contribution figure used for comparability between the two friends. The case is deliberately built around the mechanics of catching up (timing plus inflation), not around what a specific income level can or cannot afford, so this figure is fixed as a scenario constant rather than derived from a specific salary.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: This figure scales every dollar amount in the case (Priya's target balance, and both of Jordan's required contributions) proportionally, but it does not change the percent margin between the Bridge and Extended Plans (D4), nor the percent understatement from the nominal-rate trap (D5) -- those are ratios between quantities that both scale by the same factor, so they are unaffected by this assumption's exact value.

modeling_assumptions.basis: A deliberately modest, realistic delay -- not a decade, not a single year -- chosen so the Extended Plan is a genuine, comparably-weighted alternative to the Bridge Plan rather than an obviously inferior or obviously superior one.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Changing this delay changes the size of the gap between the Bridge and Extended Plans' required contributions (D4) -- a longer delay narrows the gap further, a shorter delay widens it -- without changing which plan asks for more money sooner. The delay was chosen at 2 years specifically because it lands the D4 margin at 13.66%, inside the case's 10-15% target band and well under SPEC §2's 20% cap; case.json.sensitivity_disclosure[] records this as a Category D (case-design dial), not an unstated fragility.

sensitivity_note: This case touches a real personal-finance decision (a friend's retirement savings, and a decade of a Hero's own past inaction) at comparatively low acute stakes -- a long-horizon planning choice, not illness, death, or acute hardship. FACILITATOR.md records a one-line facilitator flag per SPEC §6 for a room where a Hero's own family's retirement-savings situation might make this land more personally than expected.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA3 (the Extended Plan's 2-year retirement delay) is a case-design dial chosen by the author specifically to land the D4 margin inside the case's stated 10-15% target band and under SPEC §2's 20% cap (see modeling_assumptions[MA3].sensitivity and case.json.balance) -- not an unstated real-world fragility. Category D per skills/case-readiness/SKILL.md's disclosure taxonomy: a deliberate case-balance constant, disclosed in the open in Appendix D and case.json, not discovered after the fact.
